rationale: The board needs a cost per additional attender, so the design is a cost-effectiveness analysis alongside a controlled before-after comparison of hubs: the two group-care hubs against the four others, 2024 against 2025 to 2026, analysed by hub of booking because uptake is partial (claim c3). The trial gives the planning value for the effect (claim c1) and the costing study the expected cost drivers (claim c2). Reporting follows CHEERS 2022.
alternatives: Before-after in the two hubs only (refused: cannot separate group care from other changes)
Compare women who chose group care with those who did not (refused: self-selection)
Cost-utility analysis (refused: no utility data for pregnant women in routine records)
whyNotMoreComplex: A modelled analysis of birth outcomes would need effects the evidence does not show; attendance is the outcome the board asked about and the data record it.

decision.statement: Run a cost-effectiveness analysis of offering group antenatal care, comparing the two group-care hubs with the four other hubs before (2024) and after (2025 to 2026) the change, with the cost per additional woman attending eight or more contacts as the primary result and bootstrap uncertainty.
decision.question: What does offering group antenatal care cost per additional woman attending her recommended contacts in this service?

criteria.text: Offering group care plausibly raises attendance and costs somewhat more per woman.
Uptake is partial, so the comparison must be between hubs offering group care, not women choosing it.
The four comparison hubs changed their own antenatal pathway in 2025.

gates.requirement: Research office classification of the evaluation
gates.evidence: Service evaluation reference SEV-MAT-2026-21 dated 2026-08-05, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Finance analyst time and 2026 unit costs
gates.evidence: Finance memo FIN-MAT-2026-09, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Compare the two hubs before and after only
Cost the sessions without an attendance outcome
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from the two retrieved records; the model leads are unchecked and not used.

summary: Cost-effectiveness analysis with a controlled before-after comparison of hubs; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
